source: Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique, ASPIRE/IFAD, MAFF, Feb 2018
text:
There are two broadcasting methods for rice, chosen based on whether the field has reliable irrigation.

Wet pre-germinated broadcast (for fields with irrigation access): after the second plowing, level the soil moist, soak seed until it just shows a sprout tip (about one night plus one day), then broadcast the sprouted seed onto wet soil with only a thin water layer, ideally using a drum seeder for even distribution. Seed rate is about 80kg/ha for wet-season broadcast rice or 120kg/ha for short-duration dry-season broadcast rice. After the seed shows roughly 7-10 days of growth, bring irrigation water in gradually so the young rice roots grow strong and firm rather than being shocked by sudden flooding.

Dry broadcast (for rainfed fields with no irrigation, relying on rainfall): sun-dry the seed for 1-2 hours before sowing, then broadcast the dry seed directly onto prepared soil; it will germinate once rain arrives even after a dry spell, since the seed stays viable sitting in the soil. This method uses less seed, about 60-80kg/ha, and is typically done with a mechanical seed drill for even spacing.
